title: Chat after a connection drop
summary: The chat keeps working when its connection drops and comes back: the same composer sends again.
purpose: PiChat over the real chat controller and the real remote client, with a fictional host that can drop its stream, restart, or lose a message it had confirmed. Shows that after the connection returns the message that was waiting is settled (sent again once, never twice), the typed text is kept, and the next message goes out from the same composer.

fixture.usage: const remote = await createRemoteChat({ endpoint, fetch }); const controller = createNativeChatController({ ...remote, identity }); <PiChat controller={controller} locale="en" renderText={markdownText} />

notes: The fictional host lives in the page: `window.__ux.restart()` drops every stream and refuses requests for a second and a half, `loseNext()` makes the host confirm the next message and then lose it. The flows are the proof: the second message must go out from the same composer, and each message must show once in the thread.

flows.name: Send, the host restarts, send again

steps.expect: The text shows in the field.
The message is in the thread and the reply comes.

steps.name: restart
steps.expect: The connection drops for a moment.
The text shows in the field; nothing is lost.

steps.say: Press Enter at once, while the connection is still coming back
steps.expect: The message is taken, waits for the connection and goes out by itself from the same composer; it is answered once.

steps.say: Tap Send at once, while the connection is still coming back
steps.expect: The message is taken, waits for the connection and goes out by itself from the same composer; it is answered once.

flows.name: The host lost the message it had confirmed

steps.name: loseNext
steps.say: The host will confirm the next message and then lose it

steps.expect: The message shows at once, waiting for its reply.

steps.name: restart
steps.expect: The connection drops and comes back.
The message is sent again by itself and answered, once.
The next message goes out from the same composer.
